choice: its exit status file, or its pid reads gone and its job has not sent a heartbeat for ADOPTED_SILENCE_SECONDS
why: the box logged five live adopted runs as exited 255 in the second they were adopted, so the pid check alone misread them; the heartbeat comes from orch job run itself and does not depend on pid namespaces or /proc visibility
orch job run sends a heartbeat at most every 30 s (15 s by default); three missed heartbeats tolerate a locked orch.db without letting a dead run hold its slot for long
the next step reads again; ending a live run loses its handoff, while waiting costs one poll

why: AC2 asks for --failed only when there is no handoff; a run that leaves a marker writes its status file in a finally, so this case is only a killed runner, and #87 chose not to trust the marker without exit 0
